plain: Uncertain and unsafe, likely to fail or fall

webster.text: Depending on the will or pleasure of another; held by courtesy; liable to be changed or lost at the pleasure of another.

more.text: Uncertain; held by a doubtful tenure; depending on unknown or unforeseen causes or events.

example.quote: Imbecility in the government; discord among the provinces; foreign influence and indignities; a precarious existence in peace, and peculiar calamities from war.
example.cite: The Federalist No. 20 (Madison, with Hamilton), Dec. 11, 1787
